extracted.intended_audience: performers, artists, producers, and audiences interested in participating in or attending the Edinburgh Festival Fringe
extracted.subtask_description: Information and practical standards about the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, intended to guide artists and producers planning shows (dates, access policy, types of work showcased, and expectations about industry/media presence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Totally open access
rubrics_metrics.description: Totally open access, the Fringe is proud to include in their programme anyone with a story to tell and a venue willing to host them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fringe accepts anyone who has a show and a venue; entry to the programme is not restricted by selection panels. This openness is a core characteristic of the festival and underpins participation — artists need only have material and a host venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe Society non-vetting policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fringe Society was set up to help development but play no part in vetting the festival’s programme - a policy which remains at the core of the festival to this day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational support is provided, but the Society does not curate or approve individual shows. Performers should not expect programme-selection gatekeeping from the Fringe Society; responsibility for securing a venue and promotion largely rests with artists and producers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include anyone with a story to tell and a venue willing to host them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A willing venue is a practical precondition for being part of the programme. Artists should secure a venue partner before expecting inclusion or promotion within the festival context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of accepted genres
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fringe boasts a diverse range of shows including comedy, musicals, exhibitions and events for children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The festival explicitly welcomes many forms of live and staged work — theatre, comedy, dance, physical theatre, circus, cabaret, children's shows, musicals, opera, music, spoken word, exhibitions and events. Creators from across these genres can consider the Fringe a legitimate platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform for career development and industry exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: This festival doesn’t just attract performers and visitors from all around the world, it’s also a hotspot for creative producers and the media scouting for the next big talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fringe functions as a marketplace and discovery platform: critics, arts industry professionals, and media attend to review and book work. Artists should consider the Fringe an opportunity for reviews, bookings, networking, and being noticed by industry gatekeepers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival timing and scope
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The festival runs for a defined period each year (three weeks in August for 2026). Artists and producers must plan availability, rehearsal, run lengths, and logistics around these dates.
